subject: Marketplace private offer — annual vs multi-year prepay options and ramp schedule
messages:
From: Kate Lin <kate@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: James Ortega <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer inquiry — 3-year prepay (Acme)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re evaluating Redwood for our product AI layer and want to pursue a Marketplace private offer for either an annual or multi-year prepay. High level:
- Expected consumption: ~600M tokens/year initially, growing to ~1.2B by year 3 (ramp).
- Preferred procurement path: AWS Marketplace private offer (we need to buy through consolidated billing).
- Budget: targeting $3.0M committed over 3 years if terms/discounts align.

Questions for you: any standard term discounts for 1yr vs 3yr prepay? Can Redwood propose a ramp schedule (yearly drawdown and true-up) and confirm how overages are handled through Marketplace billing? We have an internal requirement that invoice/commitment must route through AWS Marketplace.

Attaching our short RFP. Can you share a proposed commercial structure and a Marketplace-ready private offer draft we can pass to procurement?

Attachments: ACME_RFP_20260224.pdf (PDF, 380KB)

Thanks,
Kate Lin
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — 3-year prepay (Acme)

Hi Kate — great to hear from you and thanks for the RFP. High-level options below; I’ve attached a pricing sheet with SKU-level mapping for Marketplace.

Option A — Annual prepay (preferred if you want yearly renew/start):
- Commitment: $1.1M/year
- Effective discount vs list: ~15%
- True-up: annual true-up against actual consumption; overages billed at committed rate + overage surcharge (10%).

Option B — 3-year upfront prepay (best $/token economics):
- Commitment: $3.0M paid upfront (or annual invoiced but contractually committed for 3yrs)
- Effective discount vs list: 24–28% depending on payment timing (upfront vs annual invoice)
- Ramp schedule proposal: Year1 credit draw 40% of committed capacity, Year2 30%, Year3 30% (we can model a 50/30/20 variant if you expect faster adoption)
- Marketplace notes: AWS supports multi-year private offers but they require the PO and seller acceptance flow; for upfront payments the Marketplace will process purchase orders differently — we’ll need to coordinate with the AWS Marketplace team.

Key considerations:
- Metering: we map usage to Marketplace SKUs; need to confirm expected monthly cadence so we can set proper quotas.
- Overages: options are (1) bill incremental usage via Marketplace at overage rate, (2) convert to credits applied to future months. We usually recommend credits for smoothing.
- Early termination / refunds: for marketplace private offers, refunds are governed by the AWS private offer mechanics — our legal will prepare an addendum.

Next steps: 1) I’ll draft a Marketplace-ready private offer (PDF) and a commercial summary for your procurement, 2) loop in our legal for the addendum, 3) coordinate with aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com to confirm the private offer flow and payment mechanics.

Attachments: redwood_marketplace_pricing_sheet.xlsx

If you can confirm which ramp profile you prefer (40/30/30 vs 50/30/20) and whether Acme will do upfront payment vs annual invoicing, I’ll send a formal draft.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kate Lin <kate@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private offer inquiry — metering & SKU mapping

Kate / Marissa — quick technical note from the serving/runtime side that will impact the commercial structure:

- SKU granularity: We expose separate marketplace SKUs for text-generation tokens, embeddings, and dedicated capacity (if you want reserved GPU pools as part of the commitment). If Acme plans to use embeddings heavily in Year1, we should allocate a higher portion of the committed draw to embedding SKUs to avoid mismatch in true-up.
- Billing cadence: Marketplace private offers can be structured as monthly metering (recommended) while holding a committed annual/multi-year discount. For upfront payments, the Marketplace needs explicit mapping of the prepaid amount to SKUs and months — we typically do a month-by-month credit allocation in the private offer so AWS can consume credits against metered usage.
- Overages handling: We recommend 1) convert overages to credits up to a buffer (e.g., 10% of commitment) and 2) bill any incremental over that via Marketplace metered line item. This gives procurement predictable spend while preserving accurate usage accounting.

I’ll prepare a mapping table (SKU -> expected monthly consumption by ramp profile) and share by EOD Monday.

—Vivek
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kate Lin <kate@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, James Ortega <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft private offer — legal redlines and marketplace considerations

Hi all — I reviewed the high-level commercial options and wanted to flag legal items specific to AWS private offers and multi-year prepay:

1) Refunds / early termination: AWS Marketplace private offers constrain refund mechanics; we must include an addendum that clarifies refundable credits vs non-refundable upfront payments. For a true upfront 3-year prepay we recommend classifying 80% as non-refundable commitment and 20% as refundable credits for short-term termination risk.
2) Audit & data residency: Acme requested audit rights; we can agree to SOC2 attestations and standard audit cooperation, but any audit process must be run through Redwood’s security team and scheduled in advance. Add clause referencing SOC2 report access via redwood.com/compliance.
3) Overages & true-up: The SOW should include the ramp schedule and a clear true-up window (30 days after each 12-month period). If Acme prefers monthly true-ups, costs will be higher due to more frequent reconciliations.
4) Marketplace terms: We need to ensure the private offer explicitly calls out seller acceptance, SKU mapping, credit allocation schedule, and that Acme understands AWS Marketplace will be the payment processor. Our finance team requires 45 days to process any annual invoicing contrects that are billed through AWS (to align with revenue recognition).

I’ll prepare a short addendum draft and highlight the clauses for procurement. For execution timeline: if Acme returns signed LOI by Mar 8, we can assemble the private offer and submit to AWS by Mar 10.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lin <kate@acme-corp.com>, James Ortega <procurement@acme-corp.com>, aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Mar 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial summary & next steps — Acme private offer (action required)

Hi Kate / James / AWS Marketplace team — circling back with a concise commercial summary and clear next steps so procurement can proceed.

Commercial summary (agreed intent):
- Structure: 3-year committed prepay via AWS Marketplace private offer
- Commitment: $3.0M total committed (option to pay upfront or annual invoicing; Acme to confirm)
- Discount: 26% off list for upfront payment; 24% for annual invoicing (pay-as-yearly committed)
- Ramp schedule: default 40% Yr1 / 30% Yr2 / 30% Yr3; confirm if Acme prefers 50/30/20.
- Overages: convert overages to credits up to 10% buffer; >10% billed via Marketplace metered line-item at agreed overage rate.
- Legal: Redwood will provide an addendum clarifying refund mechanics and audit access. Finance requires 45 days for marketplace invoiced annual contracts.

Attachments: ACME_Private_Offer_Draft_20260302.pdf (private-offer draft, includes SKU mapping and credit allocation)

Next steps (action items):
1) Acme procurement (James) — confirm preferred payment cadence (upfront vs annual) and ramp profile by EOD Thu Mar 6.
2) AWS Marketplace (aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com) — confirm private offer flow for a 3yr prepaid purchase and whether upfront payment can be tokenized as credits across months. Please respond with the required buyer-seller exchange flow and expected processing lead time.
3) Redwood legal (Laura) — I’ll expect the addendum and a Marketplace-ready private offer PDF; target to submit to AWS by Mar 10 once Acme confirms.
4) Marissa to submit private offer to AWS on Mar 11 once we have buyer confirmation and legal sign-off.

Kate — happy to hop on a 20-min call this week if that helps procurement move faster.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Replies: James Ortega replied (one-line ACK) and Kate confirmed they prefer upfront payment and 40/30/30 ramp in separate short responses which are captured in the HubSpot thread.
